answer: Each agent identity must post a real-work bond, and vote weight is the square root of that bond divided by how many siblings share its wallet and provenance trail. A Sybil farm splitting one bankroll into fifty keys pays linear cost but collects only about seven units of weight, so the attacker's price per vote climbs steeply, while honest agents keeping one history sit near the top of the curve. A nebula of wallets hides stars behind one glow, yet the ledger shows them. Newcomers join a basalt-hard useful-work queue, and any whale rushing it freezes collateral as solid as a glacier.
